clue.text: Compelling posh man to go beneath central part of church

indicators.note: in a down answer, going beneath means coming lower, so this piece follows
the central part of a word is its middle letters, here the middle two of church

parts.note: a gent, short for gentleman, is a man of good breeding

explanation.surface: A well-to-do man is pressed to stand below the nave of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: CHURCH has six letters, so its central part is UR; 'to go beneath' puts GENT under it in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something urgent is pressing and demands action, which is what compelling means here.

clue.text: Bird has an advertising leaflet — there's a catch in it

indicators.note: the catch is placed in it, inside the leaflet

parts.note: a flyer is a handbill advertising something
taken as written

explanation.surface: An advertising handout comes with small print hiding a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A flycatcher is a small bird that catches insects in flight.

clue.text: One looking for beer in the hold? Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: the clue first says beer goes in the hold, signalling one word placed inside another
this reverses the roles, so the hold goes inside the beer instead

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone searches the ship's hold for a stash of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a thirsty searcher; 'Quite the opposite!' tells you to swap which word sits inside which.
explanation.definitionFit: A beholder is an onlooker, as in beauty being in the eye of the beholder.

clue.text: Scrubs comb — stylist's first

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly, to scour it

indicators.note: the first letter of the word stylist is taken

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's comb gets a good cleaning before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is to scrub hard, so scours is a verb form matching scrubs.

clue.text: Breaks said to be for a drink

indicators.note: said signals a word heard rather than read

parts.note: something that snaps breaks suddenly

explanation.surface: Someone claims their tea breaks are really just excuses for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong alcoholic spirit, a kind of drink.

clue.text: What's been noted of late?

parts.note: of late reads as about the late, the recently dead: a written notice of someone's life

explanation.surface: A question about recent events worth writing down.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a published notice recording a person's death and life story.

clue.text: Those not ready for work under the railway line?

definitions.meaning: people still asleep are not yet up for the day's work
wooden or concrete beams laid beneath railway rails

explanation.surface: Lazy workers are found lying beneath the tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepers are both slumbering people and the cross-beams that support railway track.

clue.text: Kitty returns to the scene of regular upheavals

indicators.note: returning means the word for kitty is read backwards

parts.note: the ante is the stake or pool in a card game, the kitty

explanation.surface: A cat comes back to where things keep getting turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the Sicilian volcano, which erupts frequently, a site of repeated upheavals.

clue.text: About to follow upstanding American? Positive!

indicators.note: this piece comes after the other one
in a down light, upstanding means the letters read upwards

parts.note: US is short for the United States, hence American
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone confidently follows an honest American.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sure is being certain, which is what positive means here.

clue.text: He's to fire disorganised, immature female

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter, giving just he

indicators.note: disorganised letters are jumbled out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man has to sack a chaotic young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A heifer is a young cow that has not yet borne a calf.

clue.text: Rather church retained this vessel?

indicators.note: one word holds another within it

parts.note: sooner means rather, as in I'd sooner not

explanation.surface: Asks whether the church would sooner keep this boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing ship with two or more masts, a type of vessel.

clue.text: Boy appearing after a time, after grown-up weakened

indicators.note: the period comes after the grown-up
the boy's name comes after the period

parts.note: an adult is a grown-up
an era is a period of time
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad turns up late after an adult has gone soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulterated means diluted or made impure, so weakened in strength.

clue.text: Gulf partly seen in relation to rule

indicators.note: one piece appears inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only part of the word Gulf is used, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A gulf is partly understood through its relation to a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' keeps only the first two letters of the gulf, and 'seen in' slots them just after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A regulation is an official rule laid down by authority.

clue.text: Controlled way to take speed

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing
rate means speed, as in at a great rate

explanation.surface: The steady way to get up to speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate means restrained and kept within limits, so controlled.

clue.text: Complaints made after professional matches

indicators.note: this piece comes after the professional

parts.note: pro is short for professional
Tests are international cricket matches

explanation.surface: Grumbling erupts after the professional's games.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Protests are objections or complaints voiced against something.

clue.text: Hairline fracture?

parts.note: not a thin crack in bone but a line where hair is split and combed apart

explanation.surface: A tiny crack in a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: A parting is the line on the scalp where hair is divided, a break along the hair.

clue.text: Unskilled to assemble in next pier

indicators.note: the letters are to be put together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clumsy worker is told to build the next pier.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexpert means lacking skill, so unskilled.

clue.text: Hide the port!

definitions.meaning: to shelter or conceal someone, as one might a fugitive
a sheltered anchorage where ships moor

explanation.surface: An urgent order to conceal the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour is to conceal, and a harbour is a port for ships.

clue.text: Confused general leads men to defeat ultimately in "The Big Picture"

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of defeat

explanation.surface: A muddled general marches his men to defeat in an epic film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' scrambles general; 'ultimately' takes the last letter of defeat. The quoted film-title look disguises a photographic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An enlargement is a blown-up photograph, quite literally a big picture.

clue.text: The Queen needs foreign money for the mission

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: Her Majesty needs overseas cash for an assignment.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip or task undertaken on someone's behalf, a mission.

clue.text: Southern state beginning to bargain — a washout?

parts.note: WA is the abbreviation for Washington State

indicators.note: the first letter of bargain is taken

explanation.surface: A southern state starts haggling, but it all comes to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A swab is used to wash out or clean a wound or deck, so a thing for washing out.

clue.text: Wildlife trail?

indicators.note: wild letters run free in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A track left by animals in the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: To file is to walk in a line one behind another, trailing along.

clue.text: Fast runners switch and step back

parts.note: a switch is a thin whip or cane

indicators.note: back means the word step is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A jockey uses the switch and steps back from fast horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Whippets are slim racing dogs bred for speed.

clue.text: Caught with lots of paper and cosmetics

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
reams are large quantities of paper, 500 sheets each

explanation.surface: Someone is caught with piles of paperwork and make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Creams are lotions applied to the skin, a kind of cosmetic.

clue.text: Plant in circles — a better arrangement outside

indicators.note: the rearranged word goes around the circles
an arrangement puts the letters in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
two circles look like two letter Os

explanation.surface: A plant grows in rings, with a better layout around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' scrambles better, and 'outside' says that jumble surrounds the two circles; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetroot is a plant grown for its edible red root.

clue.text: Sign up before Head of State comes in

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: to enter a contest is to sign up for it

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone registers before the head of state arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Enters means goes into or comes in.
